facts: 60-second scans failed at local 14:04:24 and 14:06:12, about 36 seconds after capture_start.
SSH return path was wired; selected 5GHz phy1 was reported idle.
After the first failure, boot_id changed and uptime reset from 81073 seconds to 38 seconds at 14:05:09. This confirms one full router reboot. No later reconnection evidence confirms a second reboot.
Before failures, last health samples reported about 350 MiB available memory. This is not proof against a later rapid OOM.
Collected logread/dmesg/pstore output contains normal watchdog initialization lines, not a panic, firmware crash stack or proven watchdog reset cause.
Scanner launches airodump-ng passive band-a channel hopping with CSV/PCAP output and does not reboot the router. 24/60 seconds use the same path.
conclusion: One actual router reboot is proven. Exact cause is unresolved; continuous monitor/channel hopping and driver or firmware handling merit investigation. An SSH channel timeout is the observed consequence, not proof of the underlying cause.

references.scope: Historical monitor-mode firmware-crash report. Different conditions and versions; not evidence that this device has the same bug.

actions: Keep 24 seconds temporarily; no blind SSH timeout increase, watchdog disable, driver replacement, or claimed 60-second fix. No router changes performed.
next_evidence: Need reboot-surviving crash output or live/serial kernel logs around failure before identifying a driver fix. No physical router reproduction in this audit.
